nfl.oneThing: The Bills stayed on top of the AFC at 9–1 with a 26–9 win over the Dolphins, and their defence held Miami to 185 yards.

headlines.title: Cowboys' offence puts up 51 on the Titans
headlines.summary: Dallas beat Tennessee 51–30 and scored on all but one possession. Dak Prescott completed 28 of 33 passes for 325 yards and four touchdowns, with no interceptions, and added a rushing score. CeeDee Lamb caught 11 of 12 targets for 132 yards and a touchdown. The Titans have now lost four straight and are 1–9. The win lifts the Cowboys to 5–6.
headlines.whyItMatters: At 5–6, the Cowboys sit 1.5 games behind the last NFC playoff spot, so this result keeps them in the race.

headlines.title: AFC playoff picture shuffles after Week 11
headlines.summary: The Broncos are back to the No. 2 seed after beating the Raiders, and they have retaken the AFC West lead on a tiebreaker. The Chiefs dropped to No. 5 despite a 34–7 win over the Cardinals. The Bengals remain No. 3 and play Monday night. The Jaguars are No. 4 and still hold a large lead in the AFC South, even after losing to the Giants. The Browns, who had a bye, moved up to No. 6, and the Steelers fell to No. 7 after losing to the Eagles.
headlines.whyItMatters: The Bills (9–1) lead the conference, but the Raiders at 4–7 are 2.5 games behind the last spot, so the bottom of the bracket is still open.

headlines.title: Titans hold the top pick for the 2027 draft for now
headlines.summary: The Titans lost 51–30 to Dallas but remain on track for the first pick in the 2027 NFL Draft. The Chargers and Dolphins also fell to 1–9 in Week 11. The Chargers lost 27–24 to the Jets, and the Dolphins lost 26–9 to the Bills.
headlines.whyItMatters: Three teams at 1–9 with seven games or more still to play means the order at the top of the draft could still shift.

headlines.title: Saints' season slides to 3–7
headlines.summary: New Orleans lost 21–13 to the Bears on Sunday, its second straight defeat. Captain Justin Reid was released last week at his own request, and the Saints fired run game coordinator T.J. Paganetti. There have been offensive line injuries and kicking problems. Quarterback Tyler Shough still says the team is good and has been in every game except the Week 4 loss to Atlanta.
headlines.whyItMatters: ESPN reports the Saints effectively need to win out over their last seven games to make the playoffs, starting with the Bengals in Week 12.

teamNews.title: Mendoza's second start shows promise
teamNews.text: Fernando Mendoza threw three touchdown passes in his second career start, his first on the road, and grades were positive despite the loss. Mendoza threw one interception.

teamNews.title: Jeanty's big game
teamNews.text: Ashton Jeanty had 79 rushing yards on 11 carries and 90 receiving yards with a touchdown on five catches. Analysts picked him out as one of the positives in the loss.

teamNews.title: Bowers could return next week
teamNews.text: Coach Klink Kubiak said after the loss he is optimistic Brock Bowers (ankle and quadriceps) will be available to face the Browns on Nov. 29.

recaps.text: Denver led 17–0 early, and the Raiders climbed back to tie it before the Broncos pulled away. Jonah Coleman's three touchdowns carried Denver, and Fernando Mendoza's three touchdown passes in his second start were not enough. Ja'Quan McMillian's one-handed 35-yard pick-six with 1:52 left sealed it. It was the Raiders' seventh loss in their last eight games, and it drops them to 4–7.

recaps.text: The Giants held on after a close finish, and the defence did most of the work. Abdul Carter had two sacks and Trevor Lawrence threw two interceptions. J.J. McCarthy's touchdown pass to Malik Nabers was enough for New York. The Giants (6–3–1) remain in the NFC's top three, and Jacksonville (7–3) keeps its AFC South lead.

recaps.keyLine: Brissett 24/37, 276 yds, 1 TD, 1 INT · Henry 13 car, 94 yds, 1 TD · Young 22/30, 254 yds, 2 TD, 1 INT · Hubbard 27 car, 120 yds, 2 TD
recaps.text: Bryce Young drove the Panthers 55 yards to set up a 37-yard field goal with 1:44 left, and it was his 14th game-winning drive. Chuba Hubbard carried 27 times for 120 yards and two touchdowns, which kept Carolina in front in a game full of lead changes. Baltimore had a chance to go ahead late but could not finish. The win is Carolina's second straight and lifts it to 5–5.

recaps.keyLine: Smith 17/21, 176 yds, 3 TD · Bailey 2 sacks, 5 tkl · Herbert 15/21, 131 yds, 2 TD · McConkey 5 rec, 37 yds, 2 TD
recaps.text: Geno Smith threw three touchdown passes as the Jets won a game that was decided by three points. Justin Herbert threw two touchdowns for the Chargers, but he took heavy hits late and was placed in the concussion protocol. Ladd McConkey scored twice, and Los Angeles falls to 1–9.

recaps.keyLine: Shough 25/42, 222 yds, 1 TD, 1 INT · Olave 9 rec, 102 yds · Williams 15/23, 181 yds, 2 TD, 1 INT · Simmons 3 sacks, 4 tkl
recaps.text: Jeffery Simmons had three sacks, which matched his career best, and helped the Bears to a 21–13 win. Caleb Williams threw two touchdowns for Chicago, which moves to 8–2. Tyler Shough threw for 222 yards and a touchdown for New Orleans, but the Saints could not finish the job.

recaps.keyLine: Rodgers 30/44, 227 yds, 1 TD · Hurleman 6 rec, 61 yds, 1 TD · Milton 11/21, 141 yds, 0 TD · Barkley 17 car, 75 yds, 1 TD
recaps.text: Philadelphia pulled off an upset, beating Pittsburgh 19–16 in a close game. Saquon Barkley scored on a run, and Byron Young had two sacks for the Eagles. Aaron Rodgers threw for 227 yards, but the Steelers could not get the points they needed. Pittsburgh's postseason hopes took a hit.

standouts.why: A rookie making a case for rookie of the year honours, the 111 yards were a season best and the three touchdowns carried Denver past Las Vegas.

standouts.name: Dak Prescott
standouts.why: Prescott's 325 yards and four touchdowns with no interceptions set the tone in a 51–30 win that had the Cowboys scoring on nearly every drive.

standouts.name: Chuba Hubbard
standouts.why: Hubbard was the workhorse on the ground for Carolina, giving Bryce Young the balance he needed in the close finish.

headlines.title: Reaves moves closer to a return for the Lakers
headlines.summary: Austin Reaves was a full participant at Lakers practice on Sunday after missing four straight games with a left heel bruise. The Lakers did no live-action drills, and Reaves has been ruled out for Monday's game against the Jazz. Coach JJ Redick said Reaves is improving by the day, and the team is working on equipment changes for him. Luka Doncic is averaging a league-leading 37.2 points per game for Los Angeles, which is 14–3.
headlines.whyItMatters: The Lakers and Spurs are tied at 14–3 at the top of the West, so Reaves's timing matters in a tight early race.

headlines.title: Kings sign Gabe Vincent for depth
headlines.summary: Sacramento is finalising a deal with Gabe Vincent to fill its 15th roster spot, according to ESPN's Shams Charania. Vincent finished last season with Atlanta and has also played for Miami. The Kings have been looking for backup point guard depth since Ben Simmons tore his Achilles before the season, and they have rookie Darius Acuff Jr. at the position.
headlines.whyItMatters: Sacramento is 2–14 and 15th in the West, so the signing is about depth rather than a quick fix.

headlines.title: Sixers keep rolling in the East
headlines.summary: Philadelphia leads the East at 14–3 after five straight wins. It came back from a 17-point deficit against Orlando on Wednesday in a shorthanded win, then survived a late Bucks surge on Saturday. The Sixers have upgraded Brown, Wade and Bona to probable for Monday's game against Portland.
headlines.whyItMatters: Boston is second in the East at 11–5, so Philadelphia has a clear early lead at the top of the conference.

contextCard.title: How NBA roster spots work
contextCard.body: An NBA team carries a standard roster of up to 15 players, and a team with an open spot can add a free agent on a standard contract to fill it. Teams can also carry two-way players on separate contracts, who split time between the main roster and a development league affiliate. Sacramento's signing of Gabe Vincent is a move to fill its 15th spot.
